summary: The original renders all-black (every pixel exactly 0) in every configuration tried, with no compile or runtime error reported, so no output-level comparison is possible; the score is an 'unjudgeable' placeholder and is NOT a judgment of the port, which renders a rich, plausibly-correct animated palette pattern.
observations: Original: meanBrightness avg/min/max = 0/0/0 and motion = motionLit = 0 on EVERY run — 6 s @ 20 fps, 60 s @ 5 fps, 240 s @ 2 fps, 12 s @ 60 fps, and a --skip 1200 late window. zeroMotionFrames = 100% of captured frames in all of them.
Original blackness is literal, not dim-and-quantized: --dump at t = 0, 0.05, 1.3, 5.7, 12.9 and 19.5 s returns [0,0,0] for all 60 pixels at all six times (nonzero count 0/60 each).

meta.json reports compileError: null and runtimeError: null for the original on every run, so the engine gap is SILENT — the pattern loads and runs but emits nothing. wantsSensors: false, so this is not a dead-sensor artefact (confirmed: --sensors synth with beat120 fed still gives mean 0).
Rig is not the cause: original stays at mean 0 on the default 60 px strip, on --pixels 12, on --pixels 600, on --rig grid --grid 16x16, and on --rig cloud (5x5x5).
Seed is not the cause: seed 1 and seed 1234 both give original mean 0.

Neither side exposes any controls (meta.json controls: [] for orig and port; --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on both), so there is no dial that could be gating the original's output and no control-surface mismatch to report.

Port is alive and healthy: baseline (6 s, 20 fps) meanBrightness avg 104 (min 80, max 108), motion avg 4.2, brightnessTrend steady, zeroMotionFrames 2 of 120. It stays alive in the late window too (--skip 300: mean 74; --skip 1200: mean 78), so it neither dies nor saturates.

Port's look, from the waterfalls: a smooth full-strip colour gradient with a bright apex that sweeps back and forth across the strip, producing a clear zigzag/chevron trace in the 60 s waterfall — i.e. a bouncing or ping-ponging position combined with a continuously re-coloured gradient.

Port's colour behaviour over 60 s cycles through distinct palette families in succession — blue/magenta/white, then green/yellow/dark, then red/yellow, then blue/magenta again — with smooth blends between neighbouring pixels rather than hard steps, which is at least consistent with the pattern's name. Whether it matches the original's palettes, cadence or motion is UNVERIFIABLE, since the original produced no pixels to compare against.
Port channel means at baseline (R 97.7, G 43.2, B 171.3) confirm the blue-dominant opening regime seen in the image.
feedback: This is an ENGINE-GAP finding, not a port bug: the original .epe runs on our engine without error yet writes zero to every pixel at every time. Someone with source access should find which construct the original uses (most likely a palette/paint API or a helper the engine stubs out to nothing) and make the engine either implement it or fail loudly, because a silent all-black render is indistinguishable from a correct black pattern and defeats output-only verification.

No fidelity feedback for the port can be given from output: with the original at zero pixels, every axis (structure, motion, colour, rhythm) is unmeasurable. Do NOT read the score as a criticism of the port.

Once the engine renders the original, re-verify against these already-established port facts so the comparison is quick: port draws a smooth gradient across the whole strip with a bright apex that ping-pongs (zigzag waterfall trace), cycles through several palette families over ~60 s, and holds meanBrightness near 80-105 with motion ~4/frame at 20 fps and no decay out to t = 1210 s.
